title: Microsoft Purview Information Protection: File Labeler and File Viewer for macOS
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's macOS client announcement, rollout targets and continued application of existing label policies. The publishing-policy controls and per-user billing model are supported, and searches did not establish the client-specific details the briefing leaves open.

claims.claim: Advanced label-based protection is an endpoint DLP setting used with the information protection client.
claims.quote: When you configure users for the endpoint data loss prevention setting Advanced label-based protection for all files on devices and use the information protection client

claims.claim: On Windows, Advanced label-based protection allows encrypted non-Office, non-PDF files to retain their extension on the device.
claims.quote: When a user selects a sensitivity label that applies encryption, the file name extension now doesn't change. As a result, there's no change to the user workflow because they can continue to view and edit the file in their standard application.

claims.claim: Without that setting, encrypting those files with the Windows client changes their extension.
claims.quote: When users label and encrypt these files with the information protection client and without this setting for advanced label-based protection: ... The encrypted file changes its file name extension and becomes read-only

claims.claim: Without that setting, those encrypted Windows files open in the Information Protection Viewer instead of their original applications.
claims.quote: can no longer be opened by apps that support the original file name extension. Instead, the file opens in the Microsoft Purview Information Protection viewer.

claims.claim: Access to label-encrypted content depends on permissions in the label's protection.
claims.quote: Control access to content by using encryption for emails, meeting invites, and documents to prevent unauthorized people from accessing this data. You can also choose which users or groups have permissions to perform which actions and for how long.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The sources do not describe the macOS client's extension and application handling of encrypted non-Office, non-PDF files without Advanced label-based protection.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview macOS "File Viewer" encrypted files extension authentication supported versions; read MC1326509, information-protection-client and dlp-learn-about-advanced-label-protection. The notice mentions .pfile viewing but does not explain this macOS encryption workflow.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described the macOS client's account and sign-in experience.
claims.quote: Searched: "macOS" "File Labeler" sign-in authentication account; read MC1326509 and information-protection-client, including its Windows client Entra prerequisites. No account or sign-in instructions for the macOS clients were found.

claims.claim: The notice describes user-driven file labeling, not autonomous behavior.
claims.quote: Searched: "macOS" "File Labeler" autonomous automatic labeling; read the supplied notice and information-protection-client. MC1326509 describes users selecting and labeling files; no autonomous behavior for these macOS applications was found.

claims.claim: Supported macOS versions and system requirements for these clients are not stated in the sources read.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview macOS "File Labeler" "File Viewer" install admin block sign in system requirements; read MC1326509 and information-protection-client. Client prerequisites describe Windows; macOS Endpoint DLP and Rights Management results do not establish these apps' requirements.

claims.claim: No Learn instructions were found for restricting who installs these macOS clients.
claims.quote: Searched: "macOS" "File Labeler" restrict installation admin; Purview macOS "File Labeler" "File Viewer" install admin block sign in system requirements. Read MC1326509 and information-protection-client; results about Intune privacy settings did not document this installation control.

claims.where: Governance controls; Open questions; front matter: defaultState
claims.claim: A separate switch to allow or block the macOS clients is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "macOS" "File Labeler" admin enable disable switch; read MC1326509, create-sensitivity-labels and information-protection-client. Existing labeling policies are documented; no separate macOS client enablement switch was found.

claims.claim: Label publishing configuration starts in Microsoft Purview portal at Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies > Publish label.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Publishing policies. ... On the Label policies page, select Publish label to start the Create policy configuration.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity <policy name> -AddLabels <label names> adds sensitivity labels to the identified publishing policy.
claims.quote: The AddLabels parameter specifies the sensitivity labels that you want to add to the policy. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the label. For example: ... Name

claims.claim: Tenant label publishing policies determine which users and groups receive which labels.
claims.quote: As part of the label policy, you select users and groups to have sensitivity labels and label policy settings.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy works only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Using Set-LabelPolicy requires assigned Purview permissions.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions. For more information, see Permissions in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal.

claims.claim: The cited creating-and-publishing-labels Learn article does not mention macOS.
claims.quote: Searched: create-sensitivity-labels article text for macOS; no match. Read its publishing-policy steps and PowerShell section. The macOS applicability statement is instead explicit in MC1326509.
